back: Making a single one-off product to a customer's order, such as a wedding dress or a bridge.
Making a group of identical products together before the equipment is changed for the next batch.
Continuous production of identical products on a line, with the product moving from stage to stage without a break.
Mass output on a flexible system in which each customer chooses some features.
Capital-intensive: many machines, high fixed cost, low variable cost. Labour-intensive: many workers, lower fixed cost, higher variable cost per unit.
Only above a certain output, where the fixed cost is spread widely enough that the lower variable cost wins.
Investment, new layout, retraining, disruption of output, worker resistance and loss of flexibility.
Continuous improvement through small changes, often suggested by workers in small groups, to cut waste and improve quality.
Total cost = fixed cost + variable cost per unit × output. Unit cost = total cost ÷ output.
